source.title: Agentic coding and persistent returns to expertise
facts: Anthropic analyzed about 400,000 interactive sessions; in a typical session people made about 70% of planning decisions and about 20% of execution decisions.
Typical novice sessions triggered about five actions and 600 words per prompt, while typical expert sessions triggered about twelve actions and 3,200 words.
Verified success was 15% for novice-rated sessions and about 28-33% for intermediate or higher sessions.

centralThesis: Domain expertise is not automatically replaced by an AI Agent. Clearer goals, constraints, verification, and takeover conditions let experts safely delegate longer chains of execution.
reusableArtifact: AI Agent responsibility card: planning owner, execution authority, verification evidence, and failure owner.

chapters.title: Observe the work split
chapters.promise: Start with the observed division of labor instead of treating autonomy as a single on-or-off setting.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, separate what to do from how to execute it.
Second, delegate verifiable execution without giving away the goal.
Third, use staged check-ins to keep the direction correctable.

chapters.title: Expertise expands work
chapters.promise: Next, understand why expertise can expand the agent role instead of shrinking it.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, expertise is specific to the task at hand.
Second, precise constraints expand the agent’s useful action chain.
Third, judge progress by verifiable artifacts, not output length.

chapters.title: Allocate by risk
chapters.promise: Now divide responsibility by capability and uncertainty, not by drawing a simple human-versus-machine line.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, set delegation depth by reversibility and uncertainty.
Second, keep goals, values, and costly trade-offs with a person.
Third, define the failures and conflicts that trigger a takeover.

chapters.title: Make expertise visible
chapters.promise: Turn expertise into observable responsibility actions rather than a vague claim that an expert is present.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, encode expertise as constraints and completion evidence.
Second, correct pivotal deviations instead of trusting fluency.
Third, preserve a path to diagnose, narrow scope, and take over.

chapters.title: Use the duty card
chapters.promise: Put the principles into a four-field agent responsibility card.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, name the planning and failure owners.
Third, let agreed evidence determine whether the work is done.

factBoundaries: The study uses privacy-preserving transcript classifiers and telemetry signals; it does not directly observe real-world business outcomes.
The sample focuses on included interactive Claude Code sessions and excludes non-interactive usage.
The responsibility card is this episode’s practical synthesis, not an official Anthropic template.
inference: Organizing planning, execution, verification, and failure takeover into four fields makes the study’s decision split and expertise signals operational for viewers.
